In an extensive interview with Joanna Stern, OpenAI president Greg Brockman discusses the company's recent changes to the ChatGPT desktop app and their plan for a tabless interface. Watch the video below.

ChatGPT will one day seamlessly handle your work

A few days ago, Joanna Stern posted a teaser of an interview with OpenAI president Greg Brockman on her new YouTube channel, New Things.

Today, Stern published the full interview, covering topics like the new ChatGPT Voice, OpenAI's hardware ambitions, the Apple lawsuit, and the recent Hugging Face hack.

During the interview, Stern noted that OpenAI recently decided to merge the ChatGPT and Codex desktop apps, while also launching a new agent mode for ChatGPT called Work.

The merged interface has caused some confusion, particularly for users who just want to keep using ChatGPT and found it hard to locate their chats.

OpenAI has since updated the app, adding separate 'Work' and 'Chat' tabs at the top of the interface, as well as a dropdown menu in the left sidebar to switch between ChatGPT and Codex. While the app is now less difficult to navigate, it's still a bit unwieldy.

When asked about the misstep, Brockman agreed with Stern, admitting the new UI is 'a bit confusing,' while adding that it's 'a stepping stone toward the future,' saying the 'Work' tab will eventually disappear, with its features 'seamlessly folded into ChatGPT.'

Brockman also said that while the rollout of the merged app was confusing, OpenAI is still seeing the intended results, with Codex's user count surging from 5 million to 10 million in just a few days.

When pressed on whether that growth was simply the result of force-feeding Codex into the ChatGPT app, Brockman once again admitted so, while also pushing back, saying that was sort of the point:

The whole interview is quite interesting and definitely worth a watch. It also includes a very 'Joanna Stern' bit where she tries to work ChatGPT Voice into the conversation, and the result is... about what you'd expect.
